$comment: Named, versioned machine-verification suite for cinatra-ai/cinatra — the gate-arm half of the truthful verification-record model (the Truthful Attribution protocol §4). The truthful-attribution-gate reads THIS file at the merged SHA (authoritative, no TOCTOU) when a merge record carries a Gate-suite arm: the cited suiteId@version must equal this file's, the Accountable trailer must equal accountable{github,name,email}, and every requiredContexts entry must have concluded success on the reviewed head. highRiskPaths EXTENDS the central cinatra-ai/ci defaults (the gate verifies the effective set is a superset). High-risk changes (this file is itself one — see **/gate-suite.json in the defaults) require the HUMAN arm at tier=maintainer; the gate arm alone is rejected, so this file's birth carries a maintainer Reviewed-by, not a self-blessing gate arm. lastAuditedAt + auditEvidence are the §4 monthly-audit record; the Accountable engineer re-audits monthly and bumps BOTH coupled in one commit (the gate warns >35d, fails the gate arm >65d; the human arm is always still available).
auditEvidence: 2026-07-30 high-risk-glob pre-coverage for the exec-plane S7 service boundary (execution-plane program, lane L0 of an L0->L1->L2 sequence landing in this order deliberately): S7 lands packages/execution-plane's HTTP/mTLS service boundary (an inbound listener terminating peer-certificate auth) plus a per-command authorization voucher (the capability envelope a caller must present before the broker executes a command) — both are trust-boundary surfaces of exactly the class the existing auth-security / extension-system-architecture globs exist to catch, yet neither packages/execution-plane/src/service/** nor packages/execution-plane/src/authz/** matches any existing highRiskPath: the closest existing anchors ('**/auth/**', '**/trust-gate/**', '**/capability-registry/**', '**/transport-registry/**') are literal directory-name matches that this package's src/service/ and src/authz/ directory names do not satisfy. Verified against the CURRENT effective set (40 paths, defaults union repo globs, superset check passing) across the full PR branch tree (5,903 tracked paths, including this PR's own new test file): classifyHighRisk classifies representative future leaves under both prefixes (packages/execution-plane/src/service/http-listener.ts, packages/execution-plane/src/authz/voucher.ts) NORMAL-risk today — the effective union matches ZERO paths under either prefix, because neither directory exists yet on this branch (S7's code lands in a later lane of this same program); this PR deliberately lands gate coverage BEFORE the risk code, closing the historical evasion window the two 'Prior record' entries below both recorded in the REVERSE order (risk code landed first, coverage followed). Added TWO precise highRiskPaths (EXTENDS the central defaults; superset check unaffected — every default glob remains present): 'packages/execution-plane/src/service/**' and 'packages/execution-plane/src/authz/**'. Precision verified with the gate's OWN classifyHighRisk/globToRegExp (cinatra-ai/ci scripts/truthful-attribution-gate.mjs @5c437aa1b65acd135353e92d679c3893bde42bd3 — the SAME SHA this file's truthful-attribution requiredContexts[].pinned already carries) against the full PR branch tree (5,903 paths): the two new globs newly-classify exactly 0 paths today (N=0 — the whole-tree matched-file count is unchanged at 424 files before vs. after adding the two globs, including this PR's own new test file which itself matches no glob, i.e. no over-match anywhere in the tree) while, on the representative future leaves the S7 lane will introduce, both packages/execution-plane/src/service/http-listener.ts and packages/execution-plane/src/authz/voucher.ts classify high-risk under the new globs and a representative non-boundary execution-plane leaf (packages/execution-plane/src/workspace.ts) stays NORMAL. This one-time verification (superset check, 40->42 effective globs, 424-before/424-after, N=0) is a narrative record, run once for this audit entry — NOT re-derived by the regression suite on every CI run. The DRIFT GUARD going forward is a new regression suite at scripts/ci/__tests__/gate-suite-highrisk-execplane-globs.test.mjs (same faithful-copy-of-globToRegExp pattern as the sibling scripts/ci/__tests__/gate-suite-highrisk-token-globs.test.mjs, runs in the root Vitest gate of record via the scripts/ci/__tests__ include): it asserts the two new globs stay present in highRiskPaths and that fixed representative service/authz leaves classify high-risk while fixed non-boundary execution-plane leaves stay NORMAL — so a future rename/addition that evades the globs, or an accidental over-broadening, reds a required check. version 2026.07.7->2026.07.8 per the version-bump-on-content-change rule below; requiredContexts[].pinned, accountable, and lastAuditedAt are UNCHANGED (a highRiskPaths extension, not the monthly re-audit; the gate-engine pin was already advanced to 5c437aa1 in the immediately-prior record). Prior record (2026-07-28) gate-engine re-pin + fresh re-verification path (cinatra-ai/ci#81): the truthful-attribution caller double-pin (uses:@ AND with.ref) and THIS file's truthful-attribution requiredContexts[].pinned advance 72d0b1caa9b11e33a9ba3e65e55aae46ad844bf1 -> 5c437aa1b65acd135353e92d679c3893bde42bd3 in ONE commit: the engine matches the resolved run's referenced_workflows[] against the pinned SHA EXACTLY, so a suite pin lagging the caller uses:@ (or the reverse) fails the gate arm CLOSED on every merge. Engine delta audited across the pin range: (a) EVAL TIMING — a required context that has not CONCLUDED yet is now re-polled within a bounded window instead of being read mid-flight and called a failure (the sibling required gates start in the same second as this one), with the reusable job budget raised to cover that window so the wait can never surface as a cancelled context, i.e. the same false red by another name; (b) SELF-REFERENCE — this gate is itself one of the requiredContexts above, so its own check-run is excluded from the candidate set keyed on the Actions RUN ID and never on the context NAME, and only after its IDENTITY is proved with the same reviewed-head / check-suite / latest-attempt-job / pinned-workflow / callerPath / allowedEvents binds every other candidate must satisfy; (c) TREE + PR BINDING — exact commit/tree resolution plus a tree-equality bridge against the live qualified approvals, and the post-merge arm's PR is now resolved AUTHORITATIVELY inside the engine (the commit->PR association or the squash subject's '(#N)', each accepted only when that PR's merge_commit_sha IS this commit) instead of the previous search-based guess, which could bind the reviewed head, the approvals and the required contexts to a DIFFERENT change and then red-flag the record. config/high-risk-defaults.json is byte-identical 72d0b1ca..5c437aa, so this file's highRiskPaths superset check is unaffected; 5c437aa is a clean descendant of 72d0b1ca on cinatra-ai/ci main; the change is protected by the high-risk-path review on .github/** and **/gate-suite.json. source-leak-gate requiredContexts[].pinned is DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED at 72d0b1ca (the only source-leak delta in the range is a runner-action pin bump; that caller advances on its own audited lane). allowedEvents is DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED at [pull_request, push, merge_group] — see the re-verification note below. FRESH RE-VERIFICATION PATH, added in this same commit (.github/workflows/attribution-record-reverify.yml): re-running an old post-merge Actions run replays THAT run's original workflow snapshot and engine pin, so a merge record red-flagged by an engine defect can never clear by rerun — the replay re-executes the defective engine and returns the same verdict forever. The new workflow is dispatch-only and VERIFICATION-ONLY: it checks this repo out AT an operator-supplied merge commit (so this file, the changed-file set, the squash message and the first-parent base are all read as of that merge, no TOCTOU), checks the gate engine out at the SAME pinned SHA as the caller above, and invokes the engine's OWN post-merge CLI arm in enforce mode — the same engine, same arm, same inputs, run fresh. Its grant is read-only (contents/pull-requests/checks/actions read; no write scope), and the engine reads through API GETs only, so the job cannot mint, edit or delete any record; its entire output is the run conclusion plus the log/step summary (Actions of course creates that run and its own distinctly-named check-run — the platform reporting the job, not an attribution record). It must be dispatched from the default branch: workflow_dispatch runs the snapshot of the workflow file on the SELECTED ref, so a side-branch dispatch would run that branch's copy and its pin, not this one. It is NOT a required context and cannot become one by accident: its job carries a distinct display name, so scripts/ci/merge-group-coverage-guard.mjs still resolves 'truthful-attribution-gate / truthful-attribution-gate' to exactly ONE workflow file, and it does not call the reusable engine via uses:, so it produces no referenced_workflows[] entry to satisfy a workflow-pinned context with. allowedEvents was NOT widened to admit workflow_dispatch, deliberately: a dispatch run's check-run attaches to the head of the dispatched branch — which could in principle coincide with some PR's reviewed head — but it can never satisfy that required context on FOUR independent binds (its check-run NAME differs from the context name; its run.path differs from the declared callerPath; it references no reusable workflow, so referenced_workflows[] cannot match the pinned SHA; and workflow_dispatch is not an allowed event), so it never needs the event admitted; widening the list would instead ADMIT the shortest-but-wrong path (adding workflow_dispatch: to the required-context caller itself), where the reusable engine runs with NEITHER arm firing — its steps are guarded on pull_request / push — producing a check-run that verified NOTHING which an allowedEvents entry would then let through as a satisfied required context. version 2026.07.6->2026.07.7 per the version-bump-on-content-change rule below; lastAuditedAt is unchanged (a pin + verification-path change, not the monthly re-audit). Prior record (2026-07-20) high-risk-glob gap closure (cinatra#1856): the HMAC token mint/verify surfaces that live as flat leaves under src/lib/ (agent-run-mcp-actor-token.ts, widget-mcp-actor-token.ts, chat-mcp-actor-token.ts, agent-run-token.ts, widget-token-broker.ts, widget-chat-resume-token.ts) plus the assistants routes that mint/verify them classified NORMAL-risk — the only auth/token-adjacent globs in the effective union anchor on src/lib/auth* prefixes or **/session*, none of which match widget-*/agent-run-*/chat-* token leaf names, so a machine-arm merge of an authentication-token change was admissible with no maintainer Reviewed-by. Near-miss trigger: PR #1855 (merged as ab534e9b2) introduced src/lib/widget-chat-resume-token.ts (a distinct HMAC resume-token type, per-run jti, TTL-bound at verify, member floor by omitting the elevated-role claim) and changed both assistants routes; ALL of #1855's changed files matched ZERO high-risk globs, so the gate would have classified this authentication-token change NORMAL-risk — the exact evasion class recorded for #1289 (NONE of its changed paths matched any highRiskPath; only the reviewer's manual hold kept it gated). Added THREE precise highRiskPaths (EXTENDS the central defaults; supersede check unaffected): 'src/lib/**/*token*.ts' (covers all six token mint/verify leaves + their __tests__ siblings) and the two token-consuming route seams 'src/app/api/assistants/chat/**' and 'src/app/api/assistants/runs/**/stream/**' (a route-only change without a lib edit would otherwise still classify NORMAL, so the token-leaf glob alone is NOT sufficient). CHOSE the directory-scoped 'src/lib/**/*token*.ts' OVER the broad anti-rename pair ('**/*actor-token*' + '**/*resume-token*' + '**/*token-broker*' + '**/*-run-token*'): the broad pair escapes src/lib into the monorepo packages (packages/streams/src/token-broker.ts, packages/agents/src/__tests__/agent-run-token.integration.test.ts) — over-match outside this issue's scope that would mark unrelated packages/** edits high-risk — whereas the directory-scoped glob cannot leave src/lib, and EVERY *token*.ts under src/lib is a security token surface or its test (zero benign production matches across all 354 flat src/lib/*.ts leaves — approval-fatigue guard holds), while remaining rename-robust for the codebase's *-token.ts naming convention. Precision verified with the gate's OWN classifyHighRisk/globToRegExp (cinatra-ai/ci scripts/truthful-attribution-gate.mjs @72d0b1caa) against the ab534e9b2 branch tree: the three new globs newly-classify exactly 21 paths high-risk — the six token leaves + 8 token tests under src/lib + 7 files under the two assistant route seams (chat/route.ts, chat/capabilities/route.ts, runs/[runId]/stream/route.ts + their __tests__) — with NO over-match of any unrelated src/lib/*.ts. Regression assertion committed at scripts/ci/__tests__/gate-suite-highrisk-token-globs.test.mjs (runs in the root Vitest gate of record via the scripts/ci/__tests__ include): it reads THIS file's own highRiskPaths and, using a faithful pinned copy of the gate's globToRegExp, asserts each known token leaf + the two route seams classify high-risk and that a representative non-token src/lib leaf (drizzle-store.ts) stays NORMAL — so a future rename/addition that evades the globs, or an accidental over-broadening, reds a required check. Codex converged the glob set MERGE-SAFE (confirmed coverage + non-over-match). version 2026.07.5->2026.07.6 per the version-bump-on-content-change rule below; requiredContexts[].pinned UNCHANGED (no gate-engine/pin change). Prior record (2026-07-10) high-risk-glob gap closure (cinatra#1289 / cinatra#1293): the S0 credential-store capability-ownership GRANT primitive (cinatra#1289) is a credential trust boundary the owner reserved for security review, yet NONE of its changed paths matched any highRiskPath, so the machine gate classified it normal-risk (only the reviewer's manual hold kept it gated). The grant primitive is a flat src/lib leaf (extension-capability-ownership-grants.ts), its bootstrap DDL is an additive .ts leaf (extension-grant-schema.ts) not migrations/**|schema.sql, and the host-port grant surface it extends (extension-host-port-grants.ts) shares the same evasion — the existing extension globs anchor on capability-registry/ / trust-gate/ DIRECTORIES, which these leaves are not under. Added TWO precise highRiskPaths (EXTENDS the central defaults; supersede check unaffected): '**/extension-*grant*' (covers the grant primitive, the extension-grant-schema.ts DDL leaf, extension-host-port-grants.ts, and the existing extension-install-grant-context.ts sibling) and '**/*capability-ownership*' (anti-rename hardening for the primitive/test + the future S1 consuming resolver keeping the domain term). Precision verified with minimatch against the branch tree: the pair matches ONLY the grant leaves and their tests (7 paths) with no over-match of unrelated src/lib/*store*.ts files. DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED: src/lib/drizzle-store.ts (4564-LOC general store carrying host-port grant DDL inline) — a wholesale glob would mark every store edit high-risk (approval fatigue); the codebase's own mitigation is to EXTRACT grant DDL into extension-*grant* leaves, which the new glob covers. Codex converged the glob set MERGE-SAFE (ran minimatch to confirm coverage). version 2026.07.3->2026.07.4 per the version-bump-on-content-change rule below; requiredContexts[].pinned UNCHANGED (no gate-engine/pin change). Prior record (2026-07-06) merge_group activation (engineering#484): 'merge_group' added to the truthful-attribution requiredContexts entry's allowedEvents (pull_request/push unchanged; the engine's WF-id F1 check is opt-in and fail-closed on malformed values, so widening the array only ADMITS the new event, never weakens the existing ones), version 2026.07.2->2026.07.3 per the version-bump-on-content-change rule below; requiredContexts[].pinned values are UNCHANGED and re-verified: source-leak pinned 45826486 (a direct descendant of the merge_group-capable engine ci#59 @c3bc633 — delta is exactly ci#60, the content/diff staleness binding) and truthful-attribution pinned 0d42bca (= 45826486 + ci#63 API pagination fix; contains c3bc633). Caller triggers: merge_group added to all 5 required org-gate callers (truthful-attribution, source-leak, skills-drift, ui-design-system, secrets-required) and to crm-migration-gate (the one remaining branch-protection required context without coverage), all inert until a merge queue exists (engineering#485). Coverage guard added: scripts/ci/merge-group-coverage-guard.mjs (+ vitest suite in the root gate of record) fails CI when any mirrored required context or suite requiredContexts entry lacks merge_group coverage. KNOWN LIMIT, on record: the truthful-attribution reusable ENGINE at pin 0d42bca has no merge_group pre-merge arm — on a merge_group event the context concludes green without re-verifying the synthetic candidate (the fail-closed post-merge push arm still validates every landed record); a real engine merge_group arm + pin advance is REQUIRED before Path-A queue enablement. Audit basis: the reusable truthful-attribution-gate workflow YAML is byte-identical 83ca29ef..45826486; config/high-risk-defaults.json is unchanged 0de02f3..45826486 (the 2026.06.5 superset entries still satisfy the engine); the post-merge push arm was audited live on main (runs on every push, enforce mode fail-closed, genuine record violations red-flagged and corrected during 2026-07-02/03). 45826486 is a clean descendant of 83ca29ef on cinatra-ai/ci main; protected by the high-risk-path review on .github/workflows/** and **/gate-suite.json. version is bumped whenever the pinned content changes (suiteId@version must be immutable per content).
